report.source_text: A histologic evaluation of a biopsy specimen of the largest nodule revealed an inflammatory, granulomatous-diffuse infiltrate in the superficial and deep dermis consisting of giant cells, histiocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells (Figure 1). The Ziehl–Neelsen and Gram stains were both negative. The cultures for the anaerobic and aerobic bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli were negative, as they were the antibody tests for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A three-year-old girl presented with asymptomatic, gradually enlarging nodules on her left cheek, unresponsive to systemic amoxicillin-clavulanate. Physical examination revealed erythematous, firm, non-fluctuant nodules (1-2 cm) without lymphadenopathy. A skin biopsy showed an inflammatory, granulomatous-diffuse infiltrate with giant cells, histiocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells. Extensive microbiological workup, including Gram stain, Ziehl-Neelsen stain, cultures for bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli, and antibody tests for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis, were all negative, ruling out infectious causes. Based on these findings, Idiopathic facial aseptic granuloma (IFAG) was suspected. Treatment with topical fusidic acid and oral clarithromycin was initiated, leading to complete resolution of the lesions within two months, with no recurrence after an additional month of follow-up.

Physical examination revealed 1-2 cm erythematous, hard-elastic, moderately firm, non-fluctuant nodules with negative thermotouch and no associated lymphadenopathy.

Skin biopsy showed an inflammatory, granulomatous-diffuse infiltrate in the superficial and deep dermis, consisting of giant cells, histiocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells.

Infectious causes were ruled out by negative Ziehl–Neelsen and Gram stains, negative cultures for anaerobic/aerobic bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli, and negative antibody tests for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis.
Treatment with topical fusidic acid and oral clarithromycin was initiated.
The lesions resolved after two months and did not recur after one additional month.
